L9: # Title:Graph Irregularity via Edge Deletions
L10: 
L11: Authors:【5†Julien Bensmail】, 【6†Noémie Catherinot】, 【7†Foivos Fioravantes】, 【8†Clara Marcille】, 【9†Nacim Oijid】

L13: View a PDF of the paper titled Graph Irregularity via Edge Deletions, by Julien Bensmail and 3 other authors
L14: 
L15: 【10†View PDF】 【11†HTML (experimental)】
L16: > Abstract:We pursue the study of edge-irregulators of graphs, which were recently introduced in [Fioravantes et al. Parametrised Distance to Local Irregularity. IPEC, 2024]. That is, we are interested in the parameter Ie(G), which, for a given graph G, denotes the smallest k >= 0 such that G can be made locally irregular (i.e., with no two adjacent vertices having the same degree) by deleting k edges.
L17: We exhibit notable properties of interest of the parameter Ie, in general and for particular classes of graphs, together with parameterized algorithms for several natural graph parameters.
L18: > Despite the computational hardness previously exhibited by this problem (NP-hard, W[1]-hard w.r.t. feedback vertex number, W[1]-hard w.r.t. solution size), we present two FPT algorithms, the first w.r.t. the solution size plus Delta and the second w.r.t. the vertex cover number of the input graph.
L19: > Finally, we take important steps towards better understanding the behaviour of this problem in dense graphs. This is crucial when considering some of the parameters whose behaviour is still uncharted in regards to this problem (e.g., neighbourhood diversity, distance to clique). In particular, we identify a subfamily of complete graphs for which we are able to provide the exact value of Ie(G).
L20: These investigations lead us to propose a conjecture that Ie(G) should always be at most m/3 + c, where $m$ is the number of edges of the graph $G$ and $c$ is some constant. This conjecture is verified for various families of graphs, including trees.

L215: # trureturing
L216: 
L217: A scientific method for AI to discover truth and find its next question.
L218: 
L219: 【104†Vision】 · 【105†Film】 · 【106†Start】 · 【107†Method】 · 【108†Examples】 · 【109†Truth and computation】 · 【110†Spacetime】 · 【111†Information escape】 · 【112†Evidence】 · 【113†First run】 · 【114†Lean source】 · 【115†Book†the-omega-institute.github.io】 · 【116†Contribute】 · 【117†Licensing】
L220: trureturing develops a scientific method for AI to turn gaps in knowledge into questions, test conjectures, expose limits in its representations, and return checked results to a reusable library. Autonomous research selection remains a goal to evaluate.
L221: The name expresses true · return · Turing. Truth guides the search; verified knowledge returns as a premise for the next inquiry; computation explores the connections. We call the structure we seek the geometry of logical truth: dependencies, invariants, distinctions and the boundaries of what an observer can recover.
L222: The project combines philosophical inquiry, theory, experiments and Lean 4 formalization. Each proof establishes its exact statement under declared assumptions. The 【104†vision and research guide】 connects this work to open directions.

L182: # Readme
L183: 
L184: This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an unnamed internal OpenAI model.
L185: 
L186: As part of model development, we evaluate our models on open research problems. We expanded these evaluations after performance on our existing mathematical evaluations saturated. Some outputs build upon earlier results produced by the models.
L187: This collection includes results at different stages of verification. Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations. We will continue to update this repository with Lean formalizations as we obtain them.
L188: 
L189: Some of the unformalized results could have issues. We will endeavor to fix any such issues quickly. We are also exploring community-hosted repositories for these materials.
L190: In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data, rather than polished academic papers. We defer to the math community completely on matters of credit, precedence, and concurrent work.
L191: ## Navigating the collection
L192: 
L193: The current catalogue contains 721 manuscripts organized into 373 families. A family groups related papers, which may include a principal result, companion arguments, consequences, or alternative proofs. Each family is classified by mathematical discipline.
L194:   * Start with the 【70†overview】 for descriptions of the families.
L195:   * Use the 【66†manuscript map】 to find individual papers and their supporting materials.
L196:   * The 【73†`preprints/`】 directory contains PDFs, source files, and manuscript-specific citation and build instructions.
L197:   * The 【74†Lean library】 and 【75†formalization catalogue】 describe the available formal proofs, their associated papers, and verification configurations. See the 【76†Comparator instructions】 for additional checking instructions. The repository has ~42% top-line results formalized.
L198:   * Updates to the repo are described in the 【69†history】.
